question: Which AI agents create the most value?
html:
Which AI agents create the most value

By company, the largest value pools are Thomas Scientific (est. $3.8M a year) and Frontline (est. $3.6M), out of an est. $12.7M portfolio total. The context does not give per-agent value for most of the 45 agents, so it cannot yet rank individual agents. The Punctual Pros missed-call agent is the only single agent with a worked, sourced model (Portfolio AI-agent plan; Voice AI research).

Value by portfolio company

All figures are est. run-rate EBITDA-equivalent after ramp, built on analyst assumptions and not de-duplicated (Portfolio AI-agent plan).

Portfolio companyEst. annual valueRoadmap range (est.)
Thomas Scientific$3.84M$1.25–4.8M
Frontline$3.59M$1.5–4.2M
BPI$2.27M$0.85–3.75M
CET$1.32M$0.62–2.62M
Punctual Pros$0.88M$0.32–1.12M
Fair Harbor$0.77M$0.40–1.75M
  • Thomas Scientific and Frontline together account for about 59% of the total (est.).
  • Each company's total sits inside its roadmap range (Portfolio AI-agent plan).

Value by rollout wave

  • Wave 3, revenue agents: est. $4.19M, the largest wave.
  • Wave 2, finance: est. $3.91M.
  • Wave 1, inbound-contact and document agents: est. $2.81M. This wave has the clearest baselines and the lowest risk.
  • Wave 4, monitoring services: est. $1.77M.

Strongest single-agent case

  • The Punctual Pros missed-call and after-hours booking agent recovers an est. $1.37M a year of job revenue (Voice AI research).
  • The model assumes about 3,502 calls a month, 14.8% missed, 80% recovered, a 45% booking rate, 60% incrementality and a $1,024 average ticket.
  • Outbound membership renewal adds an est. $403k of revenue.
  • These are revenue figures, not EBITDA. Do not add them to the $0.88M EBITDA-equivalent figure for Punctual Pros.

Limits of the evidence

  • Call, ticket, invoice, quote and member volumes are analyst estimates (Portfolio AI-agent plan).
  • Most performance metrics come from self-reported vendor case studies, such as booking rates of 70–90% versus 42% for human staff.
  • The company totals are not de-duplicated, so overlap between agents may overstate value.
  • Ranking individual agents needs:
  • the full 61-item agent list with per-agent value fields;
  • system-of-record counts from each portfolio company.

Next actions

  1. Pull per-agent estimated values from the full Portfolio AI-agent plan and rank the top ten by value and by wave.
  2. Replace the assumed volumes with system-of-record counts, starting with Thomas Scientific and Frontline. They carry the most value.
  3. Get the Punctual Pros call-tracking data (volume, missed rate, booking rate, member count) to validate the missed-call model before the wave 1 launch.
  4. De-duplicate overlapping agents within each company before value is used in any growth plan or board materials.

# Which AI agents create the most value

By company, the largest value pools are Thomas Scientific (est. $3.8M a year) and Frontline (est. $3.6M), out of an est. $12.7M portfolio total. The context does not give per-agent value for most of the 45 agents, so it cannot yet rank individual agents. The Punctual Pros missed-call agent is the only single agent with a worked, sourced model (Portfolio AI-agent plan; Voice AI research).

## Value by portfolio company

All figures are est. run-rate EBITDA-equivalent after ramp, built on analyst assumptions and not de-duplicated (Portfolio AI-agent plan).

| Portfolio company | Est. annual value | Roadmap range (est.) |
|---|---|---|
| Thomas Scientific | $3.84M | $1.25–4.8M |
| Frontline | $3.59M | $1.5–4.2M |
| BPI | $2.27M | $0.85–3.75M |
| CET | $1.32M | $0.62–2.62M |
| Punctual Pros | $0.88M | $0.32–1.12M |
| Fair Harbor | $0.77M | $0.40–1.75M |

- Thomas Scientific and Frontline together account for about 59% of the total (est.).
- Each company's total sits inside its roadmap range (Portfolio AI-agent plan).

## Value by rollout wave

- Wave 3, revenue agents: est. $4.19M, the largest wave.
- Wave 2, finance: est. $3.91M.
- Wave 1, inbound-contact and document agents: est. $2.81M. This wave has the clearest baselines and the lowest risk.
- Wave 4, monitoring services: est. $1.77M.

## Strongest single-agent case

- The Punctual Pros missed-call and after-hours booking agent recovers an est. $1.37M a year of job revenue (Voice AI research).
- The model assumes about 3,502 calls a month, 14.8% missed, 80% recovered, a 45% booking rate, 60% incrementality and a $1,024 average ticket.
- Outbound membership renewal adds an est. $403k of revenue.
- These are revenue figures, not EBITDA. Do not add them to the $0.88M EBITDA-equivalent figure for Punctual Pros.

## Limits of the evidence

- Call, ticket, invoice, quote and member volumes are analyst estimates (Portfolio AI-agent plan).
- Most performance metrics come from self-reported vendor case studies, such as booking rates of 70–90% versus 42% for human staff.
- The company totals are not de-duplicated, so overlap between agents may overstate value.
- Ranking individual agents needs:
  - the full 61-item agent list with per-agent value fields;
  - system-of-record counts from each portfolio company.

## Next actions

1. Pull per-agent estimated values from the full Portfolio AI-agent plan and rank the top ten by value and by wave.
2. Replace the assumed volumes with system-of-record counts, starting with Thomas Scientific and Frontline. They carry the most value.
3. Get the Punctual Pros call-tracking data (volume, missed rate, booking rate, member count) to validate the missed-call model before the wave 1 launch.
4. De-duplicate overlapping agents within each company before value is used in any growth plan or board materials.
